newsitem.title: UK: Greenalls gains after upbeat trading news.
newsitem.headline: Greenalls gains after upbeat trading news.

text.p: Shares in Greenalls Plc were marked higher in early trading on Friday after the pubs and hotels operator issued an upbeat statement on trading in the 11 months to the end of August.
The stock -- which dropped to a year's intraday low of 545p on September 11 -- was up 16p at 580-1/2 by 0715 GMT.
Shares in Whitbread Plc were also boosted by the statement, rising 4p to 695. Others in the sector also ticked higher with J.D. Wetherspoon Plc up 2-1/2p at 10.32 stg and Bass Plc up 1-1/2p at 796.

Fraser Ramzan, analyst at Lehman Brothers, said the news confirmed the positive picture in a trading statement from Bass on Wednesday, with sales in Bass Taverns up 16 percent in the first 48 weeks of the year.
"Companies seem to be benefitting from the bouyant UK consumer which is driving volumes," Ramzan said. "There are sound implications for margins."
"The company results back in May didn't really reflect the same strength in the consumer that we are now seeing. This seems to be the beginning of a round of positive statements."
Greenalls said its pub and restaurant businesses had traded significantly ahead of last year and its accommodation businesses also had a busy summer with revenue per room well up on the year before.

The company said pre-tax profit before exceptional items was significantly ahead of last year, but was in line with its expectations. Drink sales per outlet were up 7.6 percent in the past 11 months and food sales were up 10.9 percent.
